_meta.purpose: Seed data for future mapping into the app's DemandSignal object (lib/types.ts). Not wired into lib/mock/data.ts or any app code. Research-only, per issue #4.
_meta.purposeOfThisFile: Per issue #4's Required Distinction and OBJECT_MODEL.md's demand-maturity rule, this file keeps four demand layers explicitly separate: (1) search demand, (2) buyer/commercial demand, (3) our observed funnel data, (4) paid transaction data. Layers 3 and 4 are recorded here as explicit zero-state facts -- Manufacturing OS has not launched any public surface and has zero visitor, CAD/RFQ, quote, or paid/order data. This is stated directly rather than omitted, so nothing downstream mistakes 'no row' for 'not yet measured.'

demandSignals.note: Macro industry-adoption context (not a search-demand measurement): IFR-reported figures relayed via secondary coverage state 542,000+ industrial robots installed globally in 2024 with the Americas at ~9% of that (US ~68% of the Americas share); a 2026-dated press release states US robot orders grew 6.6% in 2025. Included as directional context for why this wedge's buyer population is plausibly growing, not as a search-volume figure.

evidence.summary: World Robotics 2025 report figures relayed via secondary coverage.
US robot orders grew 6.6% in 2025 per 2026-dated press release.

demandSignals.note: Australia macro industry-adoption context (not AU-specific search-demand data): Australia's National Robotics Strategy (government, 2024) and a third-party market-research forecast (IMARC Group) sizing the Australia robotics market at ~USD 1.7B in 2025. This is market/policy-level context only -- no Australia-specific, part-type-level search or buyer evidence was found for any item in the wedge. See README.md executive summary.

evidence.summary: Australia's first National Robotics Strategy, released 2024, AU$15B National Reconstruction Fund names robotics as a priority.
Australia robotics market estimated at USD 1.7 billion in 2025, forecast to USD 6.9 billion by 2034 (third-party market-research forecast, not independently audited).
